smell: Executor.Cleanup() unconditionally deletes terraform.tfstate.backup along with tfplan/destroy.tfplan after a successful destroy. The .backup file is the operator's only built-in rollback artefact if the live tfstate is later corrupted; sweeping it on success leaves the workdir in a state where a subsequent stale-state recovery has to be reconstructed from Proxmox by hand.
severity_reason: Removing the only rollback artefact from a privilege-sensitive workdir is a recoverability regression — not data loss yet, but a foot-gun the next failure mode hits. rubric §4 ad-hoc: state-recoverability
fix_summary: Split Cleanup() into two methods: CleanupPlans() removes only tfplan + destroy.tfplan, CleanupBackup() removes terraform.tfstate.backup. Call CleanupPlans() at the existing site (destroy/helpers.go:46, proxmox/proxmox.go:147). Never call CleanupBackup() — let the operator decide. Or: keep .backup until the *next* successful run, mirroring git's reflog policy.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — phase canonical helpers should not weaken recoverability
Terraform docs: terraform.tfstate.backup is written by terraform on every state mutation as a single-step rollback
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/cleanup/infra.go:55-65 explicitly preserves terraform.tfstate.backup during cleanup, then Executor.Cleanup() removes it at end-of-destroy
must_preserve: AtomicWrite + fsync invariants in system/fs.go; the destroy-with-plan flow.

smell: StepDef has no 'already-done' precondition hook. The Orchestrator runs every step in order; on a mid-phase crash the next invocation starts from step 1 and re-runs every step (download tools, regenerate manifests, regenerate ignition, rebuild ISOs). Some steps tolerate the re-run; others (StepBuildISOs, StepUploadISOs, StepDeployIgnition) are slow or wasteful. Idempotency today is implicit per-Exec rather than declared and verified.
evidence:
type StepDef struct {
  ID         StepID
  Name       string
  Desc       string
  NonFatal   bool
  SkipWhen   func() bool   // not the same as 'already done'
  ...
  Exec       func(ctx context.Context) error
}
fix_summary: Add `ReRunSafe bool` to StepDef (default false) — every StepDef must declare it. BuildSteps panics if a step omits it. For false-marked steps, also require an `AlreadyDone func(ctx) (bool, error)` hook the orchestrator consults before Exec. Stretch: persist completed StepIDs to <workDir>/.okdctl/run-state.json (AtomicWrite, 0o600) so resume is durable across PID restarts. See roadmap state:4f69fc9d:no-resume-checkpoint.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: 'StepDef + BuildSteps is the canonical way to declare phase steps'
Twelve-factor app §disposability — processes are disposable, but only when their state is recoverable
roadmap.md §state:4f69fc9d:no-resume-checkpoint — already triaged
must_preserve: distribution.StepDef + BuildSteps canonical API per CLAUDE.md.

smell: StepCleanupBootstrap, StepVerifyKubeVIP, and StepDeployProductionDNS are all NonFatal. If StepCleanupBootstrap succeeds (bootstrap VM destroyed, terraform state mutated) but StepVerifyKubeVIP fails, StepDeployProductionDNS is skipped (gated on KubeVIPVerified). The cluster is left with bootstrap gone, VIP unverified, /etc/dnsmasq.d/ still pointing at bootstrap IP — no resume path is exposed (no `okdctl postinstall` subcommand or scoped re-run flag).
severity_reason: User-visible crash recoverability gap on the destroy seam: bootstrap is destroyed via a side-effecting tf apply, then the operator has no scoped retry path. rubric §4 ad-hoc: state-recoverability
fix_summary: Two options (roadmap state:fb54208a documents both): (a) add `okdctl postinstall --step=dns` so the DNS substep is independently re-runnable once kube-vip is healthy; (b) extend update-ingress to detect bootstrap-pointed DNS and re-run dns.DeployProduction. Prefer (b) — update-ingress already owns DNS reconciliation.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/postinstall/update_ingress.go:206-210 already handles a near-identical DNS reconciliation path
roadmap.md §state:fb54208a:postinstall-no-rollback-path
Twelve-factor app §disposability
must_preserve: NonFatal semantics on StepCleanupBootstrap (bootstrap-cleanup failure is genuinely non-blocking for cluster runtime).

smell: destroySteps() correctly carved out --skip-terraform / --skip-cleanup / --skip-firewall flags so a partial-failed destroy can be resumed. But the steps themselves do not auto-detect 'already done' state. After a successful tf.Destroy() the next destroy run still calls Init+HasState — HasState() returns false (state file absent), step skips with a Warn. Other steps (StepCleanupFiles, StepCleanupFirewall) blindly re-execute even when their target is already absent. Forces operators to combine flags rather than letting destroy converge.
fix_summary: Add a per-step AlreadyDone hook (see state:4f69fc9d). For destroy specifically: StepCleanupFirewall queries firewall backend before issuing remove; StepCleanupFiles checks workDir presence first. Today these steps already log warnings on absent targets — fold the same logic into a SkipWhen-style check so the orchestrator emits Skipped instead of Success-with-warning. Improves resume UX without changing destroy semantics.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — StepDef should encode preconditions
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/destroy/helpers.go:26 (HasState check) is the right pattern, not yet generalised
must_preserve: NonFatal semantics on every destroy step — no upgrades to fatal.

smell: CleanupBootstrap silently returns nil when terraform.tfvars is missing, with only a Warn. If a previous cleanup wiped tfvars but tfstate is still present, the bootstrap VM remains alive and StepCleanupBootstrap reports success. The orchestrator pctx.BootstrapCleaned flips to true in the calling step (postinstall/steps.go:50-52), surfacing 'bootstrap cleaned' in the Result struct and any downstream summary even though the VM is still running.
severity_reason: Misleading-success on a destructive cluster-mutation path: the Result claims BootstrapCleaned=true while the bootstrap VM is still alive. rubric §4 ad-hoc: state-recoverability
fix_summary: Either (a) return a typed error so the calling step does NOT set BootstrapCleaned=true (caller is the owner of that signal), or (b) introduce a tri-state result (cleaned / skipped / unknown) and wire postinstall/steps.go to set BootstrapCleaned only on the cleaned branch. (a) is simpler and matches the SkipWhen idiom — bootstrap.go would return a sentinel that postinstall/steps.go's OnError hook downgrades to a SkipReason without flipping BootstrapCleaned.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — `BasePhase.OcResourceExists` and existence checks are canonical
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/destroy/helpers.go:26 returns nil after warning ONLY when there is genuinely nothing to do; here the absence of tfvars does NOT mean the VM is gone
must_preserve: The defer that sweeps the bootstrap-destroy.tfplan; the targeted -target apply.

smell: destroyInfrastructure short-circuits when HasState() is false but proceeds to tf.Init() when state IS present without first checking the state's lock status (.terraform.tfstate.lock.info). On NFS / shared filesystems, a stale state lock from a crashed prior run blocks Init+Plan with an opaque error. There is no `terraform force-unlock` plumbing or hint in the error path; operators have to recognise the upstream Terraform error string and run force-unlock manually.
fix_summary: After Init failure, sniff the upstream error for 'state is locked' / 'lock.info' substrings (or stat the lock file directly) and surface a typed `*errtypes.ConfigError{Msg: "terraform state locked — re-run with --force-unlock or run 'terraform force-unlock <id>' in <dir>"}`. Do NOT auto-unlock without operator confirmation. The default local backend writes lock.info next to tfstate, so a stat()/age-check is precise.
rule_source: Terraform docs: state locking on local backend writes .terraform.tfstate.lock.info
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — typed errors via errtypes drive exit-code mapping
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/destroy/helpers.go:26 already gates on HasState; equivalent pattern for lock would symmetric

smell: Provider.Provision delegates 100% to the bpg/proxmox terraform provider for retry semantics. retrieveProvisionResult derives VM IPs from config, not from Proxmox — so eventual-consistency 'VM created but not yet listed' gaps are dodged. But there is no documented invariant ('Proxmox API mutation MUST go through terraform') so a future status-query patch could trip an unprotected 5xx/429.
evidence:
// Provision -> Init -> Plan -> Apply (all terraform); no Go-side retry
// retrieveProvisionResult uses cfg.Networking.StaticIP.Start (no Proxmox call)
fix_summary: Add an authoritative comment on proxmox.Provider header: 'All Proxmox mutation MUST flow through terraform.Executor. Direct HTTP calls are forbidden in deploy/destroy paths.' If/when status reads land, route them through internal/download's retry helper (5xx/408/429 with exponential backoff, 4xx fail-fast). roadmap.md state:48688e63:proxmox-no-retry-layer documents this.

smell: `okdctl destroy` is all-or-nothing: SkipTerraform / SkipCleanup / SkipFirewall toggles are coarse-grained 'don't run this whole step' switches, not 'only destroy these resources'. There is no `--only=vms` or `--target=master` to remove a single broken VM and re-bootstrap, which is the documented Terraform pattern for partial recovery. The bootstrap.go path already uses `-target=` internally; there is no parallel exposed at the CLI.
fix_summary: Add `--target=<resource>` (repeatable) flag that maps to terraform.DestroyOptions{Targets: ...}. Validate against an allowlist (module.okd_cluster.proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.{bootstrap,master,worker}[<n>]) so a typo doesn't widen scope. Mirror the postinstall/bootstrap.go pattern. With --target, --confirm-cluster MUST still be required so a script can't sneak past the typo guard.
rule_source: Terraform docs: -target= for surgical destroys
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/postinstall/bootstrap.go:36 uses Targets internally
Skill SKILL.md §destroy-safety: 'does destroy accept destroy only VMs or is it all-or-nothing?'
must_preserve: --confirm-cluster typo guard; the existing dry-run flow.

smell: StartWorkerVMs runs `terraform apply -var start_workers_immediately=true` against the FULL state — no `-target=` scoping. If the operator hand-edited tfvars between deploy steps (or if any other resource has drifted), this apply quietly reconciles the drift along with starting workers. The intent is 'start workers' but the blast radius is 'reconcile everything Terraform sees'. Not a blocker because the canonical flow is single-shot, but it surprises operators trying to resume a partial install.
fix_summary: Add Targets: []string{"module.okd_cluster.proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.worker"} to the ApplyOptions, mirroring postinstall/bootstrap.go:36. Same change keeps the var=true semantics but bounds the apply to the worker resource graph.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/postinstall/bootstrap.go:36 already uses targeted apply
Terraform docs: -target= as a surgical-resource boundary
must_preserve: AutoApprove on this step — workers must come up unattended after bootstrap completes.

smell: `cleanup.Execute` (Full kind) calls Terraform() AFTER WorkDirectory(), WebServer(), HAProxy(), Apache(), Dnsmasq(). cleanupTerraformEnv documents 'preserve tfstate so destroy can run' (good), but if WorkDirectory()'s removal of <workDir> partially fails midway, the operator may already have lost setup-time artefacts (kubeconfig, install-config) that are required to re-run a destroy IF tfstate is then ALSO partially removed by a future invocation. Order is correct (services down before files, files before terraform-cache); the residual gap is that there is no transaction boundary — cleanup is 'best effort across N independent removers'.
fix_summary: Two-pass cleanup: pass 1 = compute every removal target and capture an inventory snapshot to <workDir>/.cleanup-plan.json (AtomicWrite, 0o600). Pass 2 = execute removals against that snapshot. On crash mid-pass-2, the next invocation reads .cleanup-plan.json and resumes. This converts cleanup from 'best-effort' to 'declarative checkpointed'. Out-of-scope for a release fix; document the failure mode in the package doc as a known limitation.

smell: runlock relies on flock() releasing automatically on fd close — correct for SIGKILL. But the human-readable diagnostic body (PID, VERB, TIME) is only consulted via Read on conflict, never validated. If the process holding the flock is unkillable (D-state on a stuck NFS mount), the only operator recourse is to delete the lock file by hand. There is no `okdctl unlock` verb and no documented recovery path. The lock-holder identity also includes only PID — no hostname / project-root, so a shared NFS mount running flock from multiple hosts produces lock conflicts whose diagnostic is misleading.
evidence:
_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(f, "PID=%d VERB=%s TIME=%s\n", os.Getpid(), verb, time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
// No hostname; no recovery verb; 'flock' may not work over NFS
fix_summary: (a) Add hostname to the lock body so cross-host conflicts on NFS are diagnosable. (b) Document in package doc that flock() on NFS pre-v4 is advisory-only and may not enforce mutual exclusion. (c) Optional: `okdctl unlock` verb that asserts no PID matches the lock body's PID before unlinking. Skill SKILL.md §tf-state-atomicity calls out concurrent-run guard explicitly.
rule_source: man flock(2) — semantics on NFS
Skill SKILL.md §tf-state-atomicity

must_preserve: flock-based release semantics; existing typed *errtypes.ConfigError on conflict.

smell: StepBuildISOs and StepUploadISOs both run unconditionally on every setup invocation (only SkipISOs gates them). On a partial-fail-and-resume scenario, ISOs are rebuilt from scratch (slow, ~5min) and re-uploaded over SSH (also slow, multi-GB) even when the existing ones are byte-identical. There is no checksum / mtime / sha256-cache fast-path.
fix_summary: For StepBuildISOs: hash the (kargs, ignition-file-content, base-iso-checksum) tuple, write the hash to <customISOdir>/.iso-build-fingerprint, skip rebuild if fingerprint matches. For StepUploadISOs: a remote sha256 over SSH plus local sha256; skip upload when they match. Both are pure performance optimisations — no security or correctness impact, just developer-quality-of-life on partial resumes.
rule_source: Skill SKILL.md §phase-idempotency: 'does the step check already done before acting?'
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/setup/release_extract.go uses sha256-keyed downloads, same pattern
must_preserve: BuildCustomISOs / UploadCustomISOsToProxmox security guards (path traversal, ISO-cleanup hardening already in place per phase/iso_cleanup.go).

smell: cleanupTerraformEnv has the right invariant (preserve terraform.tfstate so destroy can run later) but expresses it as a comment in the filesToRemove slice rather than as a tested constant or assertion. A future refactor that adds 'terraform.tfstate' to the slice would silently break destroy recoverability with no compile-time or test-time signal.
fix_summary: Hoist the slice to a package-level var, add a unit test that asserts `slices.Contains(cleanup.TerraformFilesToRemove, "terraform.tfstate") == false`. The test names the invariant; future refactors break the test before they break destroy. Same pattern for terraform.tfstate.backup if state:4c092fce:tf-state-backup-removed-on-success is also fixed (it should also NOT be removed by cleanup).
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes — invariants codified in tests when comments alone are load-bearing
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/firewall/firewall.go:32-39 hoists OKDRequiredPorts to a package var with a documented invariant
must_preserve: The exact contents of filesToRemove (plus terraform.tfstate.backup if state:4c092fce lands).

smell: StepPrintSummary classifies the destroy as 'completed' iff len(failures)==0. But Skipped steps don't append to failures, so SkipTerraform=true (resume-after-tf-destroy) leads to the summary saying 'cluster teardown completed' even though the operator skipped the only step that touches infra. The hint 're-run okdctl destroy to retry the failed steps' is also misleading on the skip path.
fix_summary: Track skipped steps in addition to failed steps. Summary message should distinguish: (a) all attempted, all succeeded → 'cluster teardown completed', (b) some skipped → 'cluster teardown completed (skipped: terraform, firewall)', (c) some failed → 'teardown finished with non-fatal failures (...)'. The Orchestrator already records Skipped per StepResult — read it back at summary time instead of the local failures slice.
